nora.p: Quick question — Priya's PTO overlaps with the company shutdown (Dec 24-26). She used 4 hours before the shutdown and wants to carry the remaining 8 hours into next year for travel. Manager already approved the full request in Lattice. Is that carryover allowed or do we need a special approval? cc @marcus
hr-bot: Reminder: Company shutdown days are treated as regular PTO when requested. Carryover is subject to the annual 40-hour cap and applicable payroll cutoffs. Policy: https://redwood.company/policies/pto
marcus: Hi Nora — short answer: yes, carryover is possible but only up to the 40-hour cap. If the employee would exceed the cap after adding the 8 hours, we need to offer encashment per policy. Process: manager confirmation + People Ops sign-off, then we record it in HRIS for year-end processing.
lina_m: I approved the time in Lattice already. Do you want me to re-open or add a note in the request?
marcus: don't reopen. Please add a note on the Lattice entry: "split PTO due to company shutdown; employee requests carryover for remaining 8h" and @mention people-ops. That gives us an audit trail.
aaron_dev: Thanks — can you confirm timing? I need to book flights and don't want to lose the hours.
jess.payroll: Payroll note: final accrual cutoff for December is Dec 20 (all time entered & approved by managers must be posted by then). Carryover is handled after year-end; encashment (if chosen) will hit Jan 15 payroll.
nora.p: Action items: 1) Lina add the Lattice note and @people-ops, 2) Aaron confirm exact remaining hours (8h), 3) Marcus to confirm carryover eligibility and follow up if encashment needed. Marcus — can you DM me once you review?
marcus: will do. If the carryover would push Priya over 40h cap we'll offer encashment option at the standard rate; I'll draft the msg to send to Priya and her manager. :thumbsup:
hr-bot: people-ops ticket created: #PO-4721 — Marcus assigned. Link: https://redwood.company/people-ops/tickets/PO-4721
nora.p: Perfect, thanks team. I'll close this thread once Marcus confirms.
